title: Groupoid laws for schemes
statement: Let $U,R$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with morphisms $s,t:R\to U$, $e:U\to R$, $i:R\to R$, and $c:R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The predicate that these maps define a groupoid means that on every test scheme $H$ they make $U(H)$ the objects and $R(H)$ the arrows, with source $s$, target $t$, identity $e$, inverse $i$, and composition $c(a,b)=a\circ b$ when $s(a)=t(b)$. Explicitly, $s(e(x))=t(e(x))=x$, $s(i(a))=t(a)$, $t(i(a))=s(a)$, $s(c(a,b))=s(b)$, $t(c(a,b))=t(a)$, $c(e(t(a)),a)=c(a,e(s(a)))=a$, $c(i(a),a)=e(s(a))$, $c(a,i(a))=e(t(a))$, and $c(c(a,b),d)=c(a,c(b,d))$ whenever the arrows are composable. The induced operations are functorial in $H$ by precomposition.
